title: Onboard a repository into private FM_HOME conventions with at most three missing-contract questions
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-29 the captain approved a design for running firstmate-workflow on other repositories (reviewed as an artifact, then grilled on consenlabs/tokenlon-mm-agent PR #164): firstmate inspects a repository and asks at most three questions to write FM_HOME/projects/<name>/CONVENTIONS.md; every merge still goes through the captain's intent card, never auto-merge; external reviewers such as that repo's R2D2-im and BB8-im can be the review, with firstmate's own reviewer only a local pre-check; and nothing about watching may depend on firstmate remembering - scripts do it. This task is one of T-137..T-141, run in the order of their depends_on. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-139.json, is committed on this branch.

Inspect. `fm project add <owner/repo>` (and firstmate on a chat request) reads with gh: merge methods, delete-on-merge, branch protection and required checks where visible (a 404 is reported as unknown, not as none), CODEOWNERS, the PR template, CONTRIBUTING, commit style from git log, and the last 30 pull requests: authors, reviewers and whether they are bots, review states and cadence, who merges, stacked bases, comment volume, languages used.

fm-project.sh verify stops refusing a private repository or unreadable branch protection (design 15.8 withdrawn); it reports what it can read, and onboarding records the rest as unknown in CONVENTIONS.md. The files it writes live under FM_HOME (T-142).

Infer, then ask at most three questions, each with the evidence and a recommended answer; everything else is shown as inferred with its evidence for the captain to confirm or correct. The first-principles default: the captain's intent card gates every merge (land: card or handoff), never auto.

Write private FM_HOME/projects/<name>/CONVENTIONS.md with front matter land: card|handoff, review: fm|external|both, post: local|summary|check|threads|comments; prose names required checks/statuses, unknown protection and confirmation, reviewers, merge methods, deletion/retention, stacking/lease policy, commits/PRs, watch cadence/debounce, posting languages and dated captain intent. External contract/config stays private; engine registry holds approved routing metadata only. Never auto-merge.

Worker and reviewer prompts include the project's CONVENTIONS.md. The captain changes it by chat through firstmate, which reports the changed lines; firstmate re-inspects on a schedule and proposes an update when the repository's own conventions drift (a new bot, a new required approval).

Tests use recorded gh payloads shaped like consenlabs/tokenlon-mm-agent's (squash only, Drone status, two bot reviewers, a stacked PR): the inferred conventions, the three questions, the written file, a chat edit, a drift proposal. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suites themselves. Stubs answer as the real tools do (gh's JSON shapes, a GitHub review, a commit status).

External project data lives only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/{repo,worktrees,CONVENTIONS.md,tasks,design.md,state}. No private specs, worktrees, prompts, pins, evidence, mirrors or recovery data in engine state or its public tree. Private repos are accepted. Unreadable protection is unknown: require captain-confirmed project checks and policy before readiness, never infer permission or reject solely for visibility. Every GitHub operation names the project repository. Preserve self-project default and explicit-name compatibility. Never push to protected base; task-branch force-with-lease requires confirmed project policy and expected old head. Merge method, deletion, land/review/post and stacking follow CONVENTIONS.md, never hardcoded squash/delete.

Evidence: required GitHub checks and commit statuses plus six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 on the authoritative current PR head; gate 3 is retired. Workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Tests stay at most 1200 lines; shared fixtures in tests/lib/ or tests/e2e/lib/, with literal helper references. Firstmate verifies CI/gates and real acceptance; a structure check cannot prove model compliance. Commit this task spec with implementation.

Empty local onboarding supports no commit/no remote/no PR history. Inspect authorized fresh /Users/benjamin/Desktop/maker-founder; ask at most three questions only for missing product/project contract, remote owner/location/visibility and checks/merge choices. Never infer product brief, invent history or create remote without contract. Record initial-commit/bootstrap exception and authorization before protected-base rules govern subsequent tasks.
